Scoring rules S(F, y) provide a principled method for evaluating probabilistic forecasts by assigning numerical penalties to forecast distributions F relative to observed outcomes y. They generalize point forecast error measures like squared error into distributional space. A proper scoring rule ensures that truthful probabilistic forecasts minimize expected score, thus incentivizing honest reporting. In GSI, these rules serve as loss functions within Bayesian updating frameworks, enabling model calibration and selection. In GSE, they guide dynamic model switching through state transitions based on out-of-sample performance. The theoretical foundation rests on convexity of forecast classes and properness conditions ensuring consistency with true distributions. Failure modes arise when models are misspecified or when scoring rules lack strict propriety, leading to misleading comparisons.
